newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Lever Bros, Brooke Bond merge.
newsitem.headline: Lever Bros, Brooke Bond merge.

text.p: Lever Brothers Pakistan Ltd and Brooke Bond Pakistan Ltd, units of Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc, have merged, company officials announced on Tuesday.
The merged company will trade as Lever Brothers, effective from May 19, a senior company executive said.
"The merger will have a positive impact on the stock prices," Nadir Shah, chief dealer of Jardine Flemings, told Reuters.
Lever's 50-rupee stock rose two rupees to 722 and Brooke Bond's 10-rupee scrip closed five up at 170 after the merger announcement.
The two companies are considered blue chips on the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE).
Lever's paid-up capital was 499.425 million rupees ($12.35 million) and Brooke Bond's 119.529 million on the KSE a day before the merger.

Lever manufactures and markets a variety of consumer items including cooking oil, soaps, detergents and ice cream. Brooke Bond processes and markets tea, mostly imported from abroad and rice, pickles and spices.

Lever Bros paid 100 percent and Brooke Bond 302.5 percent cash dividends for the 18 months ended June 30, 1996. The two companies have changed financial years to July-June from January-December last year.
